located_point.method: ASI coordinate (Indian Archaeology 2013-14, 29 deg 06' 29" N, 75 deg 05' 50" E, as recorded in sites-located-v1.json) kept. The site was levelled for cultivation (Prabhakar and Korisettar 2017, Fig. 10 'Area completely levelled'); the composite shows sandy fields with scattered shrubs north-east of the village and no mound.

sources.result: No line measured: levelled site, no visible mound or architecture at 10 m.

notes: PERIOD FLAG: every measured line at Karanpura is Early Harappan, not Mature Harappan. The Mature Harappan houses and fortification of Karanpura appear only in a photograph and in text (IAR 2013-14, Plate 38 and PDF p. 110), so no Mature Harappan line could be measured; the source id carries the period so that the comparison can exclude it. On the Early Harappan plan of Area B, the walls of the lower building complex lie at theta -8.5 to -11.6 from the plan's compass (system lower-complex, the rule's main system by length? see systems), and the two long parallel walls crossing the area lie at -16.2 and -17.5 (system long-walls). Scale from the excavation grid labels, assumed 10 m apart.
plan_search: Plan library entry karanpura-01 (trench layout without walls); held IAR 2012-13 (PDF pp. 132-137, trench layout of another site and photographs) and IAR 2013-14 (PDF pp. 88-111: location map, contour plan with trenches, Early Harappan structural plans of Areas B and D, photographs). The Puratattva 43 file in the post-catalogue-finds sources is a three-page contents excerpt.
stated_orientation_encounters: IAR 2013-14, PDF p. 110 (printed p. 105), describes Mature Harappan walls as having a 'northwest - southeast orientation' and a northeast-southwest wall, and the fortification as running 'in a northwest to southeast direction'; met while checking captions and not used.
